extracted.intended_audience: laboratory researchers and technicians performing experimental infections in animals (bacteriology/veterinary experimental pathology)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical laboratory protocols for inoculating experimental animals by various routes and for observing, sampling, and assaying infection during life (including serology and bacteriology methods). Includes stepwise operative technique, sample collection, observation schedules and preparative details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subdural inoculation technique
rubrics_metrics.description: Stepwise operative procedure to introduce inoculum beneath the dura mater via a trephine hole in the parietal segment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anaesthetise animal and secure dorsum uppermost; shave scalp in front of ears; raise a crescentic skin-muscle flap (convexity forward) from 0.5 cm in front of one ear to same point in front of other ear and reflect it; incise periosteum and raise with blunt dissector; remove a 6 mm diameter circular piece of bone from parietal (centre of hole at intersection of median line and line joining posterior canthi); introduce inoculum with hypodermic syringe, perforate dura and deposit material immediately below membrane, taking care to avoid injuring the sinuses; replace skin flap and secure with Michel's steel clips; dress with sterile gauze and wool, seal with collodion; label specimen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intracerebral inoculation (difference from subdural)
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform as for subdural inoculation except the needle is passed into the cerebral substance before ejecting contents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After perforating the dura mater, push the needle onward into the substance of one or other cerebral hemispheres before ejecting contents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intraocular inoculation — fluid inoculum
rubrics_metrics.description: Technique for injecting fluid inoculum into the anterior chamber of the eye.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use local anaesthetic (cocaine) instilled twice (two minutes apart) and wait five minutes; have animal firmly held; select two needles to fit same syringe and sterilise; attach one needle to draw up inoculum and remove it; steady eye with fixation forceps, pierce cornea with other needle allowing aqueous to escape, then attach syringe without removing corneal needle and inject into anterior chamber; irrigate conjunctival sac with sterile saline; label.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intraocular inoculation — solid inoculum
rubrics_metrics.description: Method for depositing a solid inoculum onto the anterior surface of the iris.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use general anaesthetic (A.C.E.); anaesthetise and secure animal; irrigate conjunctival sac with sterile saline; make incision through upper quadrant of cornea with triangular keratome into anterior chamber; separate lips of corneal wound with flexible silver spatula; seize solid inoculum with iris forceps and introduce through corneal wound, deposit on anterior surface of iris; irrigate sac and cornea; release animal; label.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intrapulmonary inoculation (fluid)
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct injection of fluid inoculum into lung tissue through intercostal space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No anaesthetic; have assistant hold animal firmly (foreleg drawn up and held with ear of that side); shave axillary line and disinfect skin; thrust syringe needle boldly through 5th or 6th intercostal space into lung tissue; inject contents slowly; label.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intravenous inoculation — site selection and technique
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection of vein and safe technique for intravenous injection in different species and precautions to avoid embolism or air injection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rabbit: posterior auricular vein preferred; guinea-pig: jugular (requires general anaesthetic); monkey/dog: internal saphenous vein (distend before puncture). Prepare inoculum by filtering through sterile filter paper to remove fragments that may cause embolism. Remove air bubbles by holding syringe needle uppermost, impale filter paper on needle and press piston up to expel air; burn drops on filter paper. Technique: grasp ear at root, shave and disinfect over vein, compress vein proximally to engorge, hold syringe like a pen and thrust needle through skin and vein wall into lumen, press onward toward body (bloodstream direction), release proximal compression and slowly inject inoculum; if swelling indicates subcutaneous injection, stop and retry nearer root or opposite ear; withdraw needle and press cotton-wool over puncture; label.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preventing air embolism and particulate embolism in IV injections
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare inoculum and syringe to avoid introducing air bubbles or particulate fragments into vein.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filter fluid through sterile filter paper to remove fragments; hold filled syringe vertical with needle up, impale a piece of sterile filter paper on needle and press piston upward until all air is expelled from barrel and needle; if drops appear on filter paper, burn them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inhalation inoculation — fluid aerosol method
rubrics_metrics.description: Method of exposing animals to a sprayed fluid inoculum in a closed chamber.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place animal in closed metal box; introduce nozzle of sterilised spraying apparatus through hole and spray inoculum into box; after spraying, open box and spray animal with 10% formaldehyde to destroy any virus on fur/feathers; transfer animal to cage; thoroughly disinfect inhalation chamber; label.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inhalation inoculation — intratracheal (fluid or powdered)
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct intratracheal delivery of fluid or powdered inoculum using a tracheal tube and bellows or gravity feed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use anaesthetic (A.C.E.) and secure animal on operating table; prop open mouth with gag and draw tongue forward; pass sterilised glass tube (17 cm x 0.5 cm, terminal 2 cm slightly curved) through larynx into trachea; connect Y tubing with one branch to separatory funnel/insufflator containing inoculum and other to hand bellows; allow fluid to run by gravity or blow powdered inoculum with rubber-ball bellows; remove intratracheal tube and release animal; label. Alternative for larger animals: pass glass tubing down trachea almost to bifurcation to pour fluid or blow powdered material into lungs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intragastric inoculation — larger animals (monkey, rabbit, guinea-pig)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pass a sterilised soft rubber catheter into stomach and instill fluid/semi-fluid inoculum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secure animal ventral surface uppermost; prop mouth open with gag and draw tongue forward; sterilise soft rubber catheter (No. 10 or 8 English; No. 18 or 15 French), lubricate with sterile glycerine; pass to back of pharynx in midline and gently guide down oesophagus until past cardiac orifice — do not use force; take required dose in sterile pipette, insert pipette into open end of catheter and allow fluid to run into stomach; drop pipette into lysol; run 1 c.c. sterile saline through catheter to wash out inoculum; withdraw catheter; label.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intragastric inoculation — rodents (Mark's method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Vertical restraint and oral insertion of short oesophageal tube for intragastric dosing in rats and mice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secure animal vertically; for rat use long catch sinus forceps to hold loose skin of head; for mouse assistant grasps loose skin between ears and tail; assistant opens jaw using thin-bladed forceps as gag; moisten sterilised oesophageal tube (silk rubber, 6.5 cm) and pass into mouth downwards and slightly to side until lost in digestive tract — gentle guidance only, do not use force; take dose in syringe, insert nozzle into needle-mount on tube and force piston down; detach syringe, draw sterile water in second syringe and force a few drops through tube to wash; with one quick upward movement remove tube; label.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feeding as non-operative inoculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Administration of fluid or solid inocula by offering inoculum-soaked food items to animals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fluid inoculum: soak small pieces of sterilised bread or sop (steamed at 100°C) in inoculum and offer in sterile Petri dish or capsule. Solid inoculum: small pieces of tissue placed in sterile vessels and offered to animals; label.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of infection (criteria indicating infection has taken place)
rubrics_metrics.description: Threefold definition of experimental infection used to interpret results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Infection is considered to have taken place when: (1) death of the animal is produced as a direct consequence of inoculation; (2) inoculation causes local or general pathological changes even without death; (3) substances appear in body fluids which can be shown in vitro or in vivo to have profound and specific effects on subcultivations of the originally inoculated organism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Important factors in production of infection — Seed and Soil
rubrics_metrics.description: Conceptual criteria recognizing organism virulence and host resistance as determinants of infection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A. Seed: virulence of organism and dose of organism. B. Soil: resistance offered by cells of experimental animal. Experimenter can to an extent control organism virulence and dose (exalt or attenuate virulence); host resistance varies among species and individuals and can only be standardised by selecting animals similar in age, size, sex.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observation schedule during experimental infection
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on frequency and duration of clinical observations after inoculation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enter clinical observation immediately after inoculation and continue until death. For acute infections make general observations daily; later, or for chronic infections or apparently unaffected animals, make general and special observations at weekly intervals. If animal appears unaffected, kill with chloroform vapour at end of 2–3 months and carry out complete post-mortem.

rubrics_metrics.name: General observations to record
rubrics_metrics.description: Essential routine checks to detect infection or intercurrent disease.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspect animal daily for general appearance to detect symptoms due to experimental infection or natural intercurrent infection. Record weight each day during infection at precisely same hour, preferably just before morning feed. Record temperature daily (or more frequently) during observation and carefully chart it; note species-specific normal averages to avoid assuming pyrexia when animal shows its normal temperature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special observations — local site and lesions
rubrics_metrics.description: Focused examinations related to inoculation route and lesion accessibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine site of inoculation at least weekly and palpate neighbouring lymphatic glands. Carefully investigate any local reaction at inoculation site and other readily accessible lesions. Explore any suppurative process (subcutaneous or joints) and examine pus both microscopically and culturally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collection of fluid secretions/excretions (aseptic capillary pipette technique)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sterile method for collecting pus, serous exudates and other fluid secretions into capillary pipettes for microscopic/cultural work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open case, grasp pipette by plugged end and replace lid; attach rubber teat to plugged end to use as handle; pass entire pipette length twice or thrice through Bunsen flame; snap off sealed end with sterile forceps; compress teat, thrust pipette point into secretion, relax teat to allow filling; remove pipette, allow fluid to run up stem and seal point in flame (or seal constricted portion if present). When ready to examine, snap off sealed end with sterile forceps and eject contents into sterile capsule for cover-slip preps, cultivations, or inoculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peripheral blood examination — histological aims and sampling sites
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose and guidance for histological study of blood and selection of sampling sites per species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Histological exam directed chiefly to numbers and kinds of white cells; species differences noted. Sampling sites: veins of ear for monkey, goat, dog, cat, rabbit, guinea-pig; axillary vein in pigeon and fowl; ear vein or tail-tip (wound) for rat and mouse; frog: web of foot. Use flat Hagedorn needle size No. 8; if vein not distendable use friction, warm water, or xylol to render vein visible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of dried blood films for histology
rubrics_metrics.description: Technique for making thin blood smears suitable for staining and microscopic examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain small blood drop from selected vein; touch one end of a 3 x 1 glass slip to drop to pick up small drop; lower this slide transversely onto surface of a second slide held at about 45° and retain for a few seconds while blood spreads; draw first slide firmly and evenly along lower slide's length to leave a thin regular film (likely one cell thick); allow film to air dry, stain with polychrome blood stains, examine microscopically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bacteriological examination of blood — collection and inoculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure for withdrawing blood aseptically into all-glass syringe with anticoagulant and inoculating into nutrient broth to detect circulating organisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sterilise an all-glass syringe and draw in sterile sodium citrate solution to moisten barrel; if less than 5 c.c. blood to be withdrawn eject citrate; if more than 5 c.c. retain ~0.5 c.c. citrate to prevent coagulation. Sodium citrate recipe: sodium citrate 10 g, sodium chloride 0.75 g in 100 c.c. distilled water; sterilise by boiling. Prepare animal as for IV inoculation, introduce needle into chosen vein and slowly withdraw blood; release proximal compression and withdraw needle; remove needle from syringe nozzle and deliver citrated blood into small Erlenmeyer flask containing ~250 c.c. nutrient broth; label, incubate, examine daily until growth or until 10 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serological examination of blood — aims and control sera
rubrics_metrics.description: Detect and estimate specific antibodies by comparing experimental ('specific') serum with normal or pooled 'normal' serum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Main antibodies: antitoxin, agglutinin, precipitin, opsonin, bacteriolysin. Compare behaviour of specific serum with serum from uninoculated animals of same species ('normal' serum); use pooled serum from several normal animals to reduce individual variation. Methods require collection of blood and separation of serum by centrifugation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collection of blood for serology and serum separation
rubrics_metrics.description: Aseptic method for collecting blood into sealed pipette, centrifuging and obtaining serum for serological tests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shave dorsal surface of rabbit ear over posterior auricular vein, sterilise skin with lysol applying vigorously to render ear hyperaemic, remove lysol with ether and allow evaporation; puncture vein with sterile Hagedorn needle; use small blood-collecting pipette and hold at angle to issuing drop so blood enters; warm clean end at Bunsen flame to expel air then seal clean point; place pipette on cool surface to create negative pressure and suck blood back leaving soiled end free; seal that end in flame; mark specimen on pipette. When clotted, centrifuge with clean end downward to collect red cells and clear serum above; mark and snap pipette to obtain serum for testing. For larger quantities, invert animal after puncture to let blood drop into centrifuge tube, incubate 37°C for 2 hours then centrifuge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dilution of specific serum — tube serial dilution method
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare serial tenfold dilutions (10%, 1%, 0.1%) of specific serum using sterile test-tubes and saline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pipette 0.9 c.c. sterile normal saline into three numbered tubes (1,2,3). Remove 0.1 c.c. serum from blood pipette and mix with tube No.1 to make s.s. 10% (specific serum); remove 0.1 c.c. from tube 1 and mix with tube 2 to make 1%; remove 0.1 c.c. from tube 2 and mix with tube 3 to make 0.1%. If serum yield small use Wright's method in capillary teat pipette.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dilution of serum by means of a teat pipette (Wright's method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Capillary pipette method to prepare serial dilutions when serum yield is small, ensuring equal volumes and avoiding contamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare several Pasteur pipettes with rubber teats and mark pencil level. Draw up nine equal volumes of saline into pipette separated by air bubbles as indices. Aspirate one marked volume of serum into capillary and eject into tube marked 10% and mix thoroughly by repeatedly drawing and ejecting. Use fresh pipettes to transfer one volume from 10% tube into 1% tube, then repeat to make 0.1%. Note: saline must always be taken into pipette first, otherwise residual serum may vitiate observations; do not dilute multiple serum samples from same saline to avoid cross-contamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microscopical reaction — apparatus and preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Equipment and preparative requirement for performing microscopic (hanging-drop) serological/agglutination reactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require hanging-drop slides (two cells side by side preferred), Vaseline, cover-slips, platinum loop, grease pencil, and 18–24 hour-old bouillon cultivation of the organism to be tested. (Procedure details continue beyond this excerpt.)
